office: Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER)
subject: Warning Letter — inadequate out-of-specification investigations
content:
[SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE — fictional letter written for the WarnSync reference implementation. Not a real FDA record.]

Dear Mr. Raghunathan:

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration inspected your drug manufacturing facility from October 6 to October 17, 2025. This letter concerns significant violations of current good manufacturing practice regulations for finished pharmaceuticals, 21 CFR parts 210 and 211.

1. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications (21 CFR 211.192). Your firm invalidated forty-three out-of-specification results in 2025. In thirty-one of these investigations, the assigned root cause was "analyst technique" with no supporting evidence, and no hypothesis testing was performed. Your firm did not evaluate the impact on previously distributed batches of the same product.

2. Your firm failed to establish written procedures for production and process control designed to assure that the drug products have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess (21 CFR 211.100(a)). Your blending operation for product HCM-220 was operated at blend times outside the validated range on nineteen occasions without deviation records.

3. Your firm failed to have adequate written procedures for the cleaning and maintenance of equipment (21 CFR 211.67(b)). Your cleaning validation for the shared granulation suite did not establish maximum allowable carryover limits for the highest-potency product manufactured in that suite.

Because you manufacture drug products on behalf of other companies, we recommend that you inform each of your clients of the findings in this letter. As a contract facility you have a responsibility, together with the application holder, to assure that the products you manufacture comply with CGMP.

4. Your firm failed to establish an adequate quality control unit with the responsibility and authority to approve or reject all drug products manufactured, processed, packed, or held under contract by another company (21 CFR 211.22(a)). Your quality agreements with four client application holders do not identify who is responsible for investigating out-of-specification results, and in practice neither party performed the investigation for the twelve results referred between the firms in 2025.

5. Your firm failed to establish adequate written procedures for the review and approval of production and control records to determine compliance with all established, approved written procedures before a batch is released (21 CFR 211.192). Batch record reviews for product HCM-114 were completed on average four days after distribution of the lot.

Contract facility responsibilities. Drugs must be manufactured in conformance with CGMP. FDA is aware that many drug manufacturers use independent contractors such as production facilities, testing laboratories, contract packagers and labelers. You are responsible for the quality of drugs you produce as a contract facility regardless of agreements in place with application owners.

Conclusion and response. Within fifteen working days of receipt of this letter, respond to this office in writing. Your response should include a comprehensive, independent assessment of your firm's system for investigating deviations, discrepancies, complaints, out-of-specification results and failures, together with a retrospective review of all invalidated out-of-specification results from the previous three years.
